imageReproducibility.method: Read local article/post ledgers and generation/storage implementation; no full remote file verification or regeneration performed.

noteLedger.limitation: A body manifest records stored files; it does not prove every article has valid fixed numeric inputs or can regenerate its figures. note-only is a ledger classification, not a new remote absence test.

snsLedger.limitation: Counts are per post row; a row may contain both archived and missing assets. Missing records do not establish irreversible loss, and archived records do not establish preserved generation inputs. Drive contents were not reverified.

implementation.finding: R2 article file manifests, read-back hashes, and private historical blobs support restoring saved files.
Ranking body figures use fixed chart-data.json, input SHA and a template version. This is not a universal contract for all article categories.
Default audit checks tracked docs/31 files; verify-r2 checks public body presence and referenced backgrounds. This does not fully validate every remote chart input.
New data-card generation saves source bytes, props.json, and a manifest with input/output hashes. Its local output must still be preserved by the applicable storage workflow.
This entry point reads current R2 ranking values/item and writes source.json with source key, year and restore command. That source manifest itself does not contain the fixed numeric input values.
SNS completed media are archived to Drive with a hash; the standard asset archiver handles media files, not a universal package of renderer and numeric inputs.

findings: Two-column upper/lower chart has very small labels and values at 343px body width.
Upper-five and lower-five sections each show the same kind of combined upper/lower comparison, increasing repeated content.
Footer describes an apparel-price article as this article's source data despite the subject being prefectural income.
Top/bottom comparison labels are very small in the published mobile layout.
A red/yellow choropleth is placed after the distribution heading; top/bottom numeric annotations are small and numeric class boundaries are not readable in the normal-size view.
The explanatory text describes colors and standardized deviation scores; any palette or scale change must update that text too.
A source explanation and large e-Stat card precede the main body; detailed source material could be consolidated at the end while year, measurement location and units remain near the claim.
Ranking table and scatterplot axes, ticks and regional legend are small at normal mobile width.
The next-article area was scrolled into view: the note article card displayed blank space; DOM showed an empty iframe and the magazine card had zero height.
Footer introduces an agricultural-land-conversion article as this sunshine article's source data.
Article discusses 2023 values while linked ranking cards display 2024 values; the link introduction must distinguish updated data.
Five body images and three main analysis sections move from ten expenditure groups to individual items and corroborating statistics.
Intro and closing notes identify Nagoya City, 2024, two-or-more-person households and the simple mean of 47 cities.
Intro is dense; shortening must preserve those distinctions. Detailed mobile review of all five figures remains pending.
Six images accompany Google My Maps and Google Earth instructions; detailed screenshot readability and current product behavior still require review.
Footer repeats next-step and source-data offers for multiple different analyses rather than a single clear continuation.
Visible free part explicitly identifies audience, outcomes and data limitations.
The only body image in the visible free part is a six-row CSV sample, despite the geographic data-reuse subject. A readable result-map example is a candidate, not a requirement to add decoration.
A compact source section at the end already names original institutions, years and author's processing.
Visible free part defines straight-line 800m and distinguishes it from walking distance.
Reader/outcome headings and an end source section are already present; these elements should not be added again mechanically.
